title: How to create a diversified portfolio using only low-cost ETFs
description: Building a professional-grade portfolio with 3 tickers and 0.05% fees.
content:
You don't need a hedge fund manager or a complex web of individual stocks to build wealth. In fact, most data shows that a simple portfolio of low-cost Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) outperforms complex active strategies over the long run. The key is **Broad Market Indexing**. By owning the entire haystack rather than looking for the needle, you eliminate company-specific risk while capturing the growth of the global economy. This guide shows you how to build the 'Boglehead' 3-Fund Portfolio.

Key Takeaways

  • Total Market Coverage: You need three components: US Stocks, International Stocks, and Bonds. This covers every investable asset class worth owning.
  • Expense Ratios Matter: Costs compound against you. A portfolio costing 0.05% will leave you with significantly more money than one costing 1.00% after 30 years.
  • Self-Cleansing: Index ETFs automatically sell failing companies (like Bed Bath & Beyond) and buy rising stars (like Nvidia). You never have to manage the holdings.
  • Tax Efficiency: ETFs are structurally superior to mutual funds in taxable accounts because they generate fewer 'phantom' capital gains taxes.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The US ETF market is the most liquid and cheapest in the world. You can buy the entire US stock market (3,500+ companies) for the price of a sandwich using fractional shares.

The 3 Components

Keep it simple. Here are the tickers.

1. Total US Stock Market

Tickers: VTI (Vanguard), ITOT (iShares), SCHB (Schwab).

What it is: ~3,700 US companies. Large, Mid, and Small cap.

Role: The growth engine. Bet on the American economy.

2. Total International Stock Market

Tickers: VXUS (Vanguard), IXUS (iShares).

What it is: ~8,000 companies outside the US (Europe, Asia, Emerging Markets).

Role: Diversification. Winners rotate. Sometimes US leads, sometimes International leads. Own both.

3. Total Bond Market

Tickers: BND (Vanguard), AGG (iShares).

What it is: ~10,000 US Investment Grade Bonds (Treasuries/Corporate).

Role: Stability. Reduces volatility during stock market crashes.

Sample Allocations

  1. The Aggressive Accumulator (Age 20-35):
    - 60% VTI
    - 30% VXUS
    - 10% BND.
    Focus: Maximum growth.
  2. The Balanced Path (Age 35-50):
    - 50% VTI
    - 20% VXUS
    - 30% BND.
    Focus: Growth with some stability.
  3. The Preservationist (Age 55+):
    - 40% VTI
    - 10% VXUS
    - 50% BND.
    Focus: Income and capital preservation.
  4. Rebalancing: Once a year, log in. If stocks went up and bonds went down, sell stocks and buy bonds to return to your target percentages.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why not just S&P 500 (VOO)?

VOO is great, but VTI includes Small and Mid-cap stocks. VTI is more diversified. Historically, Small Caps have a slight return premium.

Do I need a Tech ETF?

No. VTI is already ~30% Tech (Apple, Microsoft, etc.). Buying a Tech ETF on top is just 'concentration risk'. Trust the index weighting.

Is it boring?

Yes. That's the point. If you want excitement, go to a casino. If you want wealth, be boring.
